requirements: Private owned installation and AF_UNIX control
Disconnect/restart behavior observed on the actual test host

supportedV1Intent: One operator-owned single-host native reverse proxy
HTTP/1.1 application requests, exact upload and streamed response
Verified downstream HTTPS and HTTPS upstream CA/hostname
Private local operator control and diagnostic Unix socket
unsupportedV1: Root installation or privilege dropping to another account
Arbitrary third-party dynamic modules or binary portability
Seamless TLS code migration or Continuum in production data path
All-traffic atomic cutover, full drain acknowledgement or rollback of application side effects

threatModel.prefix: New canonical owned0700 private prefix without symlink ancestors
threatModel.management: Private AF_UNIX/local only; no public admin endpoint by default
threatModel.secrets: Operator-owned TLS files/state/backups stay private; evidence contains allowlisted counts/hashes only
limits: Hashes are unsigned consistency checks, not signatures
Same-UID attacker can alter files and records
Uninterruptible filesystem/kernel stalls exceed user-space elapsed budgets

health.application: Dedicated idempotent application readiness endpoint, explicit expected status/body and freshness

resources.nativeRSSGrowthMethod: Median last300seconds minus median first300seconds after warmup; master plus all observed native workers
resources.cpuScope: Master plus all observed native workers; client/application/controller measured separately

comparative.baseline: Unchanged pinned native baseline compiled with matching applicable modules, worker count, TLS and application settings on the same host; only native request-path comparison
comparative.relativeSpreadFormula: (max-min)/arithmeticMean of the two positive baseline means

runtimeAcceptance.freezeRule: Version/hash this profile, release candidate, fixture and host metadata before measurement. A changed threshold starts a new candidate; preserve the earlier adverse result. No lowering thresholds to relabel the same run.

recoveryBoundaries.configRollback: Only the explicitly managed fragment and supported durable journal/state boundaries; application effects are not undone
recoveryBoundaries.packageRollback: Separate new private prefix and retained known-good package/config/state; prove state compatibility before switching
recoveryBoundaries.libraryDrift: Refuse new start/mutation, inspect then create fresh compatible installation; never modify host libraries
recoveryBoundaries.faultedOrOrphan: Refuse automatic restart/uninstall; inspect exact owned process identities and retained records using a reviewed runbook
recoveryBoundaries.unsupportedStorage: Conflicting/unknown files, symlinks, ambiguous state and unverified identities fail closed; no automatic recursive repair

releaseRequiredEvidence: Exact source/tree/upstream and actual build checkout
Declared dependency ABI with actual package/library/Node identities
Final native/Unix/feature-off compatibility jobs actually executed
Permanent versioned archive, archive and payload hashes, licenses and dependency inventory
Independent nonroot download-to-operation replay outside checkout
Separate config and package rollback plus backup/restore failure controls
Frozen60minute normal/slow run and comparative/adverse evidence
Independent security review and residual issues
Accurate versioned release notes and product card

currentCapabilityObservation.localHost: UID0 and Node24 observed during contract preparation; not the target nonroot Node22 host
currentCapabilityObservation.existingHosted: Ubuntu24.04/Node22 native compatibility evidence exists; it is not accepted V1 service deployment
